policy_question.question: Reach floor is >=10,000. Record as '209K' cited (a) or 'unknown' (b)?
policy_question.reasoning: The floor is satisfied by two orders of magnitude under any rounding interpretation (209k implies >=208,500). The figure is creator-attested on her own official page — a single authoritative source, not the conflicting third-party abbreviations (87.1K/81.8K/82.5K) that sank the prior candidate. Recording '209K' as cited is consistent with the dataset's own followers_approx convention, which already carries K-abbreviated cited values. Recording 'unknown' would discard verified information and be inconsistent with the rest of the dataset. Limitation noted: it is rounded to the nearest thousand, not an exact integer.

claims.claim: Recent activity: Instagram travel posts on/after 2026-06-18, verifiable without login.
evidence: https://mylifesamovie.com/tag/travel-guide/ — HTTP 200, fetched 2026-09-17. Page HTML contains 9 unique instagram.com post/reel URLs (e.g. https://www.instagram.com/reel/DdWcGJ0oBuO/, https://www.instagram.com/reel/DdT0lerozrC/).

Feed items on her own domain show relative dates: '2 days ago' x1, '1 week ago' x1, '2 weeks ago' x4, '3 weeks ago' x2. Anchored to fetch date 2026-09-17, the oldest is ~2026-08-27 — all after 2026-06-18.

Captions are travel content: Zambezi River zipline ('crocodiles and hippos that also live in the Zambezi River'), Great Wall of China, Balkans roadtrip itinerary offer ('Follow @mylifesatravelmovie, one of the first original solo travel influencers').
claims.limitation: Instagram's anonymous embed endpoint (instagram.com/reel/<id>/embed/captioned/) returns HTTP 200 and exposes the caption but no longer exposes an absolute post timestamp to anonymous fetchers. The date bound therefore rests on (relative label rendered server-side on her own domain + fetch date). This is creator-attributable (her domain, her WP Instagram widget, direct instagram.com URLs) — materially stronger than the third-party 'recency' signal previously rejected — but it is a bound, not an absolute timestamp.

claims.claim: Itinerary: 'Ultimate Balkans Roadtrip Travel Guide for Luxury Adventurers' is a published structured guide dated in-window (>=2024-09-16).
evidence: https://mylifesamovie.com/ultimate-balkans-roadtrip-travel-guide/ — HTTP 200, real guide: ~13,500 words, 36 day mentions, not a stub.

Two-signal date: WordPress API https://mylifesamovie.com/wp-json/wp/v2/posts?search=Balkans returns date '2026-08-24T15:12:24' for that link; page JSON-LD BlogPosting datePublished '2026-08-24T15:12:24+00:00', dateModified '2026-09-10T09:55:45+00:00'. Both in-window.

conditions: Record followers_approx as '209K' with source cited (mylifesamovie.com/work-with-me/, fetched 2026-09-17) — NOT 'unknown'. Rationale in C2 policy answer.

Record the recent-activity evidence as the dated bound it is: IG posts ~2026-08-27 to ~2026-09-15 per (relative label + 2026-09-17 fetch), with the instagram.com post URLs preserved as the directly-verifiable artifacts.
Extract the itinerary from https://mylifesamovie.com/ultimate-balkans-roadtrip-travel-guide/ (WP API date 2026-08-24, JSON-LD agrees).
method: Fresh-context evidence-only review. Claim packet only; every claim re-fetched and checked against the cited source. No research notes or transcripts seen.
notes: No Instagram login was used or needed; all evidence came from her own domain, press profiles, and public embeds.

The '209k' figure, while rounded, comes from the single most authoritative possible source (the creator's own media page) and clears the 10,000 floor by ~20x. The prior quarantine turned on conflicting third-party estimates, a materially different evidentiary situation.
